task_name: the plan's review watch is no longer wired, started or recovered

rubric.result: The objective promises two things and the diff produces both with production lines. (a) "nothing starts a watch over the plan's issue any more": start-plan-route.ts drops the `reviews` argument, the `PlanReviewStarts` type and both `reviews.start(...)` calls (single and listed paths); active-plan-recovery.ts drops the `reviews` field and `this.reviews.startRecovered(watch)`, so `#recover` ends that branch with `this.sessions.remember(watch)` alone exactly as the brief's prose asks; implement-plan-route.ts drops `reviews.stop(...)` and the `PlanReviews` type; api-server.ts drops the `reviews` collaborator, its field, its constructor parameter and the `PlanReviews`/`WatchedIssue` types; ct-api.ts drops `#planReviews`, the `planReviewLog` local and both `reviews` arguments; plan-agents.ts and cmux-plan-agents.ts lose `review()`; read-changes-asked.ts, review-plan.ts and reviews-spy.ts are deleted. (b) "the surviving watch is the pull request's": `CtApi.#pullRequestReviews` is context-only in the diff and still wired into both `ActivePlanRecovery` and `ApiServer`, and `active-plan-recovery.ts` still calls `this.pullRequestReviews.startRecovered(watch)` from `#rememberImplementing`. Nothing the objective names is left unproduced.

The TDD line asks for `it('a_started_plan_leaves_no_watch_over_its_issue')` in `api-server.test.ts`, asserting that after a `POST /start-plan` the session is remembered and no collaborator was asked to watch the issue. The diff adds that test in that file, over that input (`RunningApi.accepted(port)` = a real POST to /start-plan through a listening server), asserting `expect(response.status).toBe(202)` and `expect(sessions.known()).toEqual([StartPlanSpy.WATCH])` — the session remembered, against the same expected value. The second half of the sentence ("no collaborator was asked to watch the issue") is fixed by construction: `RunningApi.server` no longer passes any `reviews` collaborator, so a surviving `reviews.start(...)` would throw inside the async handler and the 202 would never arrive — which is also why the test is red today, as the plan states. That structural form was the plan's own choice, since the same task deletes the spy that could have recorded the call.

The `Contract (backend/src/domain/ports/plan-agents.ts)` block asks that `review()` be gone while `launch`, `resume` and `fix` keep their four named arguments and types: the diff removes exactly the `review({ agent, issue, repository, changes })` method with its `must implement review(...)` message and leaves `resume` and `fix` byte for byte. The `Current state (ct-api.ts, 309-315)` block's `#planReviews` is removed whole. Symbol by symbol against §2's "What goes in Task 4, file by file": ct-api.ts loses `#planReviews` and the `planReviewLog` local (the remaining single consumer now reads `CtApi.#readPlanProgress(git, new MemoryReviewLog())`, which is still needed because `ReadPlanProgress` keeps its `reviewLog` collaborator until Task 6); api-server.ts loses the `reviews` collaborator, field and `PlanReviews` type; start-plan-route.ts loses the argument, the `PlanReviewStarts` type and both `start` calls; active-plan-recovery.ts loses the field and `startRecovered`; implement-plan-route.ts loses the argument and `reviews.stop(...)`; plan-agents.ts and cmux-plan-agents.ts lose `review()`. §2's "What `ImplementPlanRoute.handledBy` ends as" is matched literally: `handledBy(implementPlan, pullRequestReviews, activePlans, implementationStarts, stderr)`, in that order, and the `#accept` call site follows it.

Rows the diff bears on: D-8 (the plan review retires) — implemented, not reopened. "What goes in Task 4, file by file" — implemented file by file (see contrato). "What `ImplementPlanRoute.handledBy` ends as" — the exact five-argument order. "What `ReviewWatch` loses | only `refresh()` ... `start`, `startRecovered`, `stop` ... stay exactly as they are, because the second wiring is protected" — review-watch.ts is not in the diff at all, so `stop` survives with no caller, which is what the row orders rather than an oversight. "Which suite covers the surviving watch ... No task may modify it" — pull-request-review-loop.test.ts is absent from `## Files changed` and its verification `git diff 7f35b98 --stat` came back empty. "Where the two halves of a contract move together" — this task changes no wire contract (the /start-plan response body is untouched), so no frontend half was owed. No row is implemented with a value other than the one it states.

Exemplars: `implement-history-route.test.ts` (the outside-in route test with its doubles) is the shape the edited route tests keep — the new `PullRequestWatchSpy` is declared inside its single consumer, exactly as that file declares `ReadImplementationHistorySpy`, and it is a strict improvement on the deleted shared `ReviewsSpy` under `conventions/testing.md` ("A double doubles what its name says and nothing more" and "What several test types of the same module share lives in a type they inherit from, not ... in a shared module imported from one place only"): it implements only `start`, the whole of the `PullRequestReviews` type. `external-tools-route.ts` and `read-implementation-progress.ts` are only shrunk-around, not contradicted. Rules read: `conventions/style.md` — no comment or docstring added anywhere in the diff, every identifier English, every added function is a method (`PullRequestWatchSpy.start`); `conventions/architecture.md` — the direction of dependencies is unchanged and only narrowed (a port method, its adapter method and two use cases leave together), no new concept is smuggled into an old file; `conventions/simplicity.md` — the diff only removes, and every removal is a symbol whose last caller left with it; `conventions/decisions.md` — no rule is duplicated, and the two halves of no cross-process contract move here. `conventions/defects.md`, rule by rule: **closed vocabulary** — no subject; no value that classifies anything is introduced, and no dispatch gains a catch-all (`ImplementRequestOutcome` is untouched by this diff). **Raw map as the return value of logic** — no subject; nothing added returns or receives a map, the spy records `PlanWatch` value objects. **Two fields that have to agree** — no subject; no field, flag or sentinel is added, and the one coupling removed (the `planReviewLog` shared between the watch and `ReadPlanProgress`) reduces rather than adds. **An error named for where it happens** — no subject; no error is added, and the `must implement review(...)` message leaves with its method. Two declarations rather than findings: (1) `PlanAgentBrief.reviewErrandFor` (backend/src/infrastructure/plan-agent-brief.ts:52) loses its last production caller with `CmuxPlanAgents.review()`, which is a `conventions/simplicity.md` burden ("a public symbol ... answers to a call that exists"), but `plan-agent-brief.ts` is not in this task's `**Files:**` and Task 5's §7 text only promises it drops "the two sentences that end with `${PlanIssueBody.CHANGES_LINE}`" — the implementer could not touch it without breaking scope, so the burden is the plan's to discharge and is left to a person. (2) The slice's own `### Out of scope` already declares the same for `MemoryReviewLog`/`ReviewLog.lastAskedAt`. Skills/documents loaded: the eight ct documents from `plugin/conventions/` and `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` all loaded fine.

Every weakened or removed pre-existing assertion traces to this task's own `**Tests:** Removed on purpose` line. api-server.test.ts: the `RunningApi.reviews.started` assertion inside the listed-request test and the two tests whose only assertion was that spy (`a_plan_that_started_is_put_under_watch...`, `a_start_that_was_refused_puts_nothing_under_watch`) — covered by "the `RunningApi.reviews.started` assertions". active-plan-recovery.test.ts: six `recovered.reviews.startRecovered` expectations and three test renames that follow them — covered by "the plan-watch recovery assertions"; in every one of those tests the surviving assertions (phase, `sessions.known()`, `plans.inFlight` called once) are kept unchanged. implement-plan-route.test.ts: `accepting_the_implementation_stops_watching_the_plan_because_that_gate_is_closed`, `a_refused_request_to_implement_lifts_no_watch` and the `reviews.stopped` line inside the renamed refusal test — covered by "the `reviews.stopped` assertions", and that renamed test keeps its 400 and its `implementationStarts.remember` / `pullRequestReviews.started` assertions. cmux-plan-agents.test.ts: the whole `CmuxPlanAgents asking a parked agent for changes` describe and the double's review pieces — covered by "the `review()` cases of `cmux-plan-agents.test.ts`". The two deleted application suites are named in the same line. No assertion is relaxed that the brief is silent about, and nothing in pull-request-review-loop.test.ts was touched.

The behaviour the objective promises is produced by production code, not by scaffolding: the watch stops being started because `start-plan-route.ts`, `active-plan-recovery.ts`, `implement-plan-route.ts`, `api-server.ts` and `ct-api.ts` no longer hold a plan-review collaborator, and the port and adapter no longer declare `review()`. The two new tests are observation points over that: revert the production hunks of this diff and `a_started_plan_leaves_no_watch_over_its_issue` never sees its 202 (the route would call `start` on an absent collaborator) and `a_recovered_plan_being_written_is_remembered_as_a_session_and_nothing_watches_its_issue` fails inside `recover()` for the same reason. No hard-coded expected value or double stands in for a production line.

Inside the declared files the diff writes only what the task asks for: removals of the plan-review wiring, plus one addition — `PullRequestWatchSpy` in implement-plan-route.test.ts — which is forced by the task's own `backend/__tests__/reviews-spy.ts (delete)`, since that file's `pullRequestReviews` double was the deleted spy. Everything `### Out of scope` protects is intact: `CtApi.#pullRequestReviews` appears in the diff as context only and still carries `log: new MemoryReviewLog()`; `ReadFixesAsked`/`RequestFixes` and their imports are untouched; `pull-request-review-loop.test.ts` is not among the changed files and its verification diff was empty; no go-protocol module, no `GATES.plan`, no frontend file and no route registration other than the argument lists is touched, and `POST /implement-plan` stays mounted. The plan file carries two hunks and I rule on them separately. (1) The implementer's amendment adds `external-tools-route.test.ts`, `implement-history-route.test.ts` and `implement-progress-route.test.ts` to this task's `**Files:**`. Justified: each of those three files builds an `ApiServer` with `reviews: new ReviewsSpy()` and imports `../reviews-spy.ts`, which this task's own sentences delete along with the `reviews` collaborator, so `npm --prefix backend run typecheck` — one of this task's own `**Verification:**` commands — cannot pass without them; the edit inside each is exactly the two lines that name the deleted module and nothing else. The amendment only adds routes, removes none, and leaves this task's `**TDD:**`, `**Tests:**` and `**Verification:**` byte for byte. (2) The rest of the plan hunk is the conductor's trim of Task 3's prose, made to hold that task inside the plan contract's one-page limit. It does not look wrong: Task 3 is already committed, and the trim leaves its `**Verification:**` block untouched, keeps its TDD test name and assertion ("the route answers 202 and `RunningApi.spy.asked` holds the request; red today") and lists the same set of removed test names, only shortening the justification clauses; the one substantive change, replacing the literal `ImplementRequestOutcome` object in Task 3's `Contract` block with a four-line comment naming the same eight members, weakens a contract block for a task that has already been implemented and judged, and disarms no control of this task or that one. Its only residue is a double blank line before Task 3's `**TDD:**`.

Two tests are added. `a_started_plan_leaves_no_watch_over_its_issue` (api-server.test.ts): deterministic — no clock, no randomness, no sleep, a real server on port 0 and a temporary frontend root; isolated — it builds its own `PlanSessions()` and the suite's `afterEach` stops every server it started, taking nothing from the order of the file; verifies real behaviour — the assertion is on the status of a real HTTP response and on what the real `PlanSessions` holds, and it goes red if the production hunks are reverted. `a_recovered_plan_being_written_is_remembered_as_a_session_and_nothing_watches_its_issue` (active-plan-recovery.test.ts): deterministic and isolated — it builds a fresh `fixture()` of doubles with no shared mutable state and no I/O; verifies real behaviour — `expect(recovered.sessions.known()).toEqual([IN_FLIGHT])` is on the real registry after a real `recover()`, and it recovers the identity dimension that the deleted `reviews.startRecovered` expectation used to carry. Two notes below the blocking three, left as notes rather than findings: its name joins two clauses with `and`, which the loaded `control-tower-loop:test-driven-development` skill discourages ("Minimal | One thing. 'and' in name? Split it."), but the plan dictated that exact name in its `**Tests:** added:` line, so it is the plan's call and not the implementer's; and the renamed `a_plan_the_agent_would_not_take_starts_no_pull_request_watch_or_implementation_start` still bundles two expectations, which it already did before this diff and which the rename describes more honestly than the name it replaced.
